decisions.reason: A same-message MODIFY already records the requirement that the power system support both motors, solenoid valves, and cooling fans under load; no additional propagation is needed.
The electrical load-capacity decision does not change the whisk head's size, material, style, or positioning requirements.
Power-system load capacity does not alter the existing splash-control target or methods; the source message's splash discussion is a separate clause from the audited source Event.
Requiring adequate electrical capacity under combined load does not change the established 3000 RPM maximum or variable-speed behavior.
The power-capacity requirement does not modify the expected smoothness, foam quality, or high-speed mixing behavior.
Electrical capacity under load has no necessary effect on quick or tool-free whisk detachment.
Although solenoids contribute to electrical load, the source Event does not change the valve mechanism, button actuation, or dispensing behavior.
The electrical load-capacity constraint does not change bowl capacity, form, size, or refilling preferences.
Supporting the electrical components under load does not alter the plumbing seals, closed-valve drip behavior, or leak-containment requirements.
The capacity requirement may influence power-supply selection but does not necessarily change the established off-the-shelf component strategy or custom spout strategy.
Electrical capacity under combined load does not change bowl removal, clearance, or event-swapping behavior.

The basic wiring-plan deliverable remains required unchanged; determining its detailed response to the load constraint requires engineering work rather than propagation of a new client-defined attribute.
